title_line: Founder and Licensed Clinical Social Worker
bio_p1: Rachel's path to becoming a therapist and founding Pathways Within was shaped by her own experiences with loss, resilience, and the power of community. After losing her father as a child, she was supported by a strong village of family, teachers, mentors, and friends. Those experiences helped shape her belief that healing often begins with feeling safe, understood, supported, and most importantly that no one has to navigate difficult experiences alone.
bio_p2: In her clinical work, Rachel helps individuals and couples explore their experiences, strengthen communication, and create healthier relationships with themselves and others. She specializes in anxiety, depression, PTSD, couples counseling, hypnotherapy, veterans and first responders, and weight-loss surgery evaluations and counseling. That same belief in whole-person, collaborative care ultimately grew from a private therapy practice into Pathways Within.
bullet_1: Rachel's own experiences with loss, resilience, and the support of a strong community shaped her belief that healing is rooted in connection and that no one should have to navigate difficult seasons alone.
bullet_2: In her work with individuals and couples, she helps clients explore their experiences, feel safer and more grounded, strengthen communication, and build healthier relationships with themselves and others.
bullet_3: Rachel specializes in anxiety, depression, PTSD, couples counseling, hypnotherapy, veterans and first responders, and weight-loss surgery evaluations and counseling, bringing a thoughtful, collaborative approach to each client's path forward.

He has a particular love for working with what he affectionately calls "neuro-spicy" minds, appreciating the creativity, intensity, and individuality that often come with ADHD. Clients often appreciate his approachable style, genuine curiosity, and ability to balance warmth, humor, and structure, creating an environment where trust can grow and lasting change feels possible.

bio_p1: Madeline may enter the room with a youthful, fresh energy, but beneath that brightness is a woman who has already lived many lives. She has known family violence and teen dating violence, not only through study but through personal experience as well. For a long time, she did not even know there were words for what she had been through, let alone that help existed. She served as an EMT for five years, including through COVID, while going to school, working, and carrying enormous stress, health challenges, burnout, and profound loss in a very short span of time.
bio_p2: Her path into therapy was through a calling that kept revealing itself. In substance use treatment, a women's group became a trauma group, showing her how deeply survival, addiction, violence, and healing are intertwined. Through human services, school-based programs, working with veterans, children, survivors of interpersonal violence, those dealing with domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking, Madeline discovered that trauma was not just something she studied. It was something she understood with humility, heart, and profound depth. Grounded in CBT, psychoeducation, and a growing passion for mind-body healing, she is building a practice rooted in compassion, courage, and the belief that people can care for others without abandoning themselves...they can survive, rebuild, and become completely whole again.
bullet_1: Madeline carries the rare wisdom of someone who has lived through trauma, loss, burnout, service, and healing...still choosing purpose, hope, and humanity.
bullet_2: From EMT work through COVID to substance use, trauma groups, schools, domestic violence, sexual assault, human trafficking, veterans, children, and survivors of violence, she has met emotional pain in almost every form.
bullet_3: Today, she helps people know they can care for others, without abandoning themselves, and that healing is truly possible.

bio_p1: Sofia's path to clinical care began with a curiosity about people and the forces that shape their behavior. After studying forensic psychology and exploring a future in law and criminal justice, she realized she was drawn less to what happens after people reach a breaking point and more to understanding what they are experiencing along the way. Graduate school at Adelphi helped turn that curiosity into a calling, while supportive professors and a close clinical internship helped shape the kind of provider she wanted to become.
bio_p2: Today, Sofia works with children, adolescents, young adults, and adults navigating anxiety, negative self-talk, relationships, changing life stages, and the everyday challenges that can feel overwhelming. With children, she uses play to understand how they experience their world; with parents, she helps connect what a child is experiencing to what happens at home and is building out a piece of her practice, navigating and guiding families through their entire dynamics and challenges. With adults, she offers space to slow down, be heard, and make sense of what comes next. Whether someone is three or forty-three, Sofia meets them with genuine curiosity: Help me understand what it's like to be you and in this space you can express all of you, completely.
bullet_1: Sofia brings curiosity, playfulness, and genuine clinical skill to her work with children, adolescents, young adults, and adults navigating anxiety, relationships, life transitions, negative self-talk, and the moments when life simply feels overwhelming.
bullet_2: Drawing from CBT, DBT, motivational interviewing, and play therapy, Sofia helps people make sense of what they're thinking and feeling, develop healthier coping strategies, and discover new ways to move forward, with children, parents, and adults all having a meaningful part in that process.
bullet_3: She creates a place where a child can play, a parent can better understand, or an adult can finally let everything out without fear of judgment. She listens for what's underneath the words, meets people where they are, and helps them feel understood enough to begin seeing themselves differently, and maybe even possibilities they didn't know were possible.

bio_p1: Colm works with people who are searching for a deeper connection with themselves, whether they are navigating a major life transition, feeling creatively stuck, questioning their path, or experiencing a sense that something is missing beneath the surface. His approach combines Internal Family Systems (IFS/parts work) and somatic therapy to help clients better understand their inner world, build self-compassion, and move forward with greater clarity and confidence. He is especially drawn to working with people who value reflection, spirituality, creativity, and exploring healing from a more holistic perspective.
bio_p2: Before becoming a therapist, Colm spent years exploring the connection between mindfulness, creativity, and personal growth through work in media, yoga, meditation, and environmental education. Those experiences shaped his belief that healing happens when we can honor both the science of mental health and the wisdom found in our bodies, relationships, and the natural world. Today, he brings that integrated perspective into his work, creating a space where clients can feel understood, grounded, and empowered to discover what comes next.
bullet_1: Colm blends Internal Family Systems (IFS/parts work) and somatic therapy to help clients navigate life transitions, creative blocks, and moments when they feel disconnected from themselves or their purpose.
bullet_2: With a background spanning media, yoga, meditation, and clinical social work, he brings together science, spirituality, and practical tools for meaningful change.
bullet_3: He is especially passionate about helping clients reconnect with themselves, nature, and what matters most.

bio_p1: Long before she became a therapist, Ren was the person carrying the weight others couldn't. A survivor of trauma, domestic violence, sexual assault, and a traumatic brain injury, she knows firsthand what it feels like to wonder if you'll ever make it through. Yet from those experiences emerged an unshakable belief: healing is possible. Once she found the courage to pursue the calling she had carried since childhood, she completed Stony Brook University's accelerated social work program, earning both her bachelor's and master's degrees in just three years before dedicating herself to serving survivors, adolescents, families, and individuals facing life's hardest moments.
bio_p2: Today, Ren brings together clinical expertise and profound humanity. She has supported survivors of domestic violence, rape, sexual assault, and human trafficking, worked alongside forensic teams during crisis response, guided adolescents through mental health and substance use challenges, and cared for loved ones through Alzheimer's, schizophrenia, and physical disability. Her mission is simple but powerful: to ensure every person she meets feels seen, heard, valued, and capable of creating a future they once thought was impossible.
bullet_1: • Whether working with adolescents, adults, couples, or older adults, Ren helps people reclaim their voice, rediscover their worth, and remember that their story is not defined by what happened to them, but by what they choose to become.
bullet_2: • After surviving trauma, violence, loss, and some of life's darkest moments, Ren dedicated her life to helping others find the strength, healing, and hope they may have forgotten still exists within them.
bullet_3: • With specialized experience supporting families, and survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, rape, human trafficking, PTSD, complex trauma, anxiety, and depression, she brings both professional expertise and the rare gift of truly understanding what it means to fight your way back.

bio_p1: Tiffany has spent more than 20 years caring for people in almost every kind of circumstance; from hospital patients and people in outpatient care to individuals navigating the correctional and shelter systems. Along the way, one thing that has stayed with her is that you can't understand someone's mental health by looking only at their symptoms. The relationships they're in, the environment in which they live, their culture, their habits, and the pressures they carry all matter. That perspective shapes the way Tiffany works with every patient who sits across from her.
bio_p2: As a psychiatric nurse practitioner, Tiffany works with adolescents and adults who want more than a quick prescription and a return visit. She believes medication can be an important part of treatment, while also helping people build the changes, skills, and support that make lasting improvement possible. Coming from a cultural background where mental health was not always openly discussed, she is especially passionate about creating space for people to talk honestly without shame or judgment. Her goal is to help patients manage their symptoms, yes. Even more so, it's to help them feel healthier, more present, and able to truly enjoy their lives again.
bullet_1: Over 20 years of nursing experience across hospital, outpatient, correctional, and psychiatric settings has taught Tiffany that every diagnosis comes with a person, a story, and a life beyond the exam room.
bullet_2: Psychiatric nurse practitioner serving adolescents and adults, with a whole-person approach that integrates medication management, lifestyle changes, coping skills, and emerging treatment modalities.
bullet_3: Born into a legacy of nurses and shaped by crisis, culture, and compassion, Tiffany is changing how mental health is understood, especially in communities where suffering was once endured in silence.

Her work includes medical massage, manual lymph drainage, pregnancy massage, deep tissue, somatic techniques, orthopedic massage, and more. bio_p1: Danielle understands that what we carry doesn't always stay in our minds. Stress can become tension. Overwork can become pain. An injury, headache, or persistent ache can affect far more than one part of the body. Having experienced the impact of high stress herself, Danielle discovered practices that helped her reconnect with a sense of balance, and ultimately found a calling in helping others do the same.
bio_p2: For Danielle, there are no shortcuts when it comes to understanding and caring for the body. After completing an intensive two-year clinical massage program and more than 1,100 hours of classroom and clinical training, she built her experience in spas, wellness centers, chiropractic clinics, and private practice before returning to New York. Today, after 12 years in the field, she brings her skills to Pathways because she believes massage belongs in a broader, holistic approach to wellness. Whether someone is navigating chronic pain, injury, stress, or simply the tension of everyday life, Danielle meets them with patience, knowledge, and deep respect for the trust they place in her. Years from now, she knows she will look back and know how many people she helped feel better, how many allowed her to be part of their journey, and those she has been privileged to serve and guide toward a healthier mind, body, and soul.
bullet_1: Danielle is a clinically trained massage therapist who sees the body as a whole, because pain, tension, injury, and stress rarely exist in isolation.
bullet_2: With 1,100+ hours of clinical and classroom training and dual licensure in New York and Connecticut, she draws from deep tissue, trigger point, Swedish, sports massage, and acupressure techniques.
bullet_3: Most importantly, Danielle considers every client's trust an honor, and every step toward feeling better a journey she is privileged to share.

bullet_1: Leonard combines traditional acupuncture expertise with a deep understanding of the connection between physical, mental, and emotional wellness.
